summary: [Private] Scheduled backups failing with AccessDenied to S3 (backup CronJob)
description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports scheduled backups failing since enabling the new scheduled backup CronJob.
- Failure is consistent across retries with AccessDenied when writing to object storage.

Impact
- No successful backups for ~24 hours.
- Customer is in a change window preparing for an upgrade and is blocked by “backup before upgrade” gate.
- RPO risk: elevated (no recent snapshot).

Customer context
- Helix Financial Software (Private deployment, regulated workload).
- Backup target: Amazon S3 bucket in customer AWS account with SSE-KMS.
- Cluster: Kubernetes in VPC (private subnets). S3 access via VPC endpoint.

Environment
- Redwood Private version: 1.18.3 (per customer)
- Backup tooling: rw-private-dr scheduled CronJob installed via Helm
- Storage backend: S3
- Encryption: SSE-KMS (customer-managed key)

Steps to reproduce (customer)
1) Install/enable scheduled backups via Helm values (backup.schedule.enabled=true).
2) Wait for CronJob to create Job.
3) Job fails ~10–30s after start.

Observed behavior
- Job pod exits non-zero.
- Logs show AccessDenied on PutObject to S3 prefix.

Expected behavior
- Backup artifacts uploaded to s3://<bucket>/<prefix>/... and job reports success metric.

Error logs (from customer, redacted)
- Pod: rw-private-backup-20251126-020000-5q9gz
- Namespace: redwood-private

Primary error:
"upload failed: s3://helix-rw-private-backups/prod/cluster-a/2025-11-26T02:00:05Z/manifest.json An error occurred (AccessDenied) when calling the PutObject operation: Access Denied"

Additional context:
"Using server-side encryption: aws:kms (keyId=arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:***:key/***)"

Also observed (intermittent depending on artifact):
"An error occurred (AccessDenied) when calling the GenerateDataKey operation: Access denied"

Notes
- Customer confirmed network path to S3 is OK (other workloads can read/write the bucket).
- Customer confirmed the role associated with the backup Job is assumed successfully via IRSA.

Support request
- Please advise required IAM permissions + bucket/KMS policy adjustments for rw-private-dr backup CronJob using SSE-KMS, and how to validate quickly.
comments:
2025-11-26 09:14 (Markus Klein, Solutions) — Opened on behalf of Helix. They’re blocked on their upgrade because “scheduled backups must be green.” They enabled scheduled backups yesterday; first run failed with AccessDenied. Customer is asking for the exact IAM policy we expect for S3 + SSE-KMS.

I asked them to provide:
- Backup bucket name + prefix (ok to redact account id)
- KMS key ARN + whether key is in same account
- ServiceAccount name/role ARN used by backup Job
- Pod logs from latest failed Job
2025-11-26 10:02 (Rafael Mendes, SRE) — Triage: this matches our common failure mode for S3+SSE-KMS where PutObject is allowed but KMS GenerateDataKey/Encrypt is missing (or key policy doesn’t trust the role). The intermittent GenerateDataKey AccessDenied in the log strongly suggests missing KMS permissions or key policy trust.

Requested from customer:
- `kubectl -n redwood-private get sa -o yaml | grep -A5 eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn`
- bucket policy (redacted)
- key policy (redacted)

Also suggested quick local validation:
- Run one-shot: `rw-private-dr backup verify --target s3 --check perms` (if installed) OR use AWS CLI with `--sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id ...` while assuming the same role.
2025-11-26 11:20 (Markus Klein, Solutions) — Customer provided details:
- IRSA role: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/helix-rw-private-backup
- Bucket: helix-rw-private-backups
- Prefix: prod/cluster-a/
- KMS key is in same account, key policy currently only allows the account root and a separate “platform-admin” role.
- Current IAM policy on helix-rw-private-backup includes s3:PutObject/GetObject/ListBucket on bucket + prefix, but no kms permissions.

They also confirmed the Job uses `--sse-kms-key-id` (SSE-KMS enabled).
2025-11-26 11:44 (Rafael Mendes, SRE) — Root cause confirmed: backup role missing KMS permissions AND KMS key policy does not allow the IRSA role principal.

Provided remediation (customer action items):
1) Update IAM policy attached to `helix-rw-private-backup` role to include:
- `kms:Encrypt`
- `kms:Decrypt` (needed for restore verification and some read paths)
- `kms:GenerateDataKey`
- `kms:DescribeKey`
Scoped to the specific key ARN.

2) Update the KMS key policy to allow the same role to use the key.

3) Confirm bucket policy allows `s3:PutObject` with `s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption` = `aws:kms` and `s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id` = key ARN (if they enforce conditions).

Shared internal reference: Terraform module in `redwood-terraform` PR 318 includes the baseline least-privilege policy; recommended copying that structure.

Also noted: If they require bucket policy conditions, ensure the client is setting SSE headers (we do) and that their condition keys match.
2025-11-26 13:07 (Markus Klein, Solutions) — Customer updated IAM role policy to include kms actions (Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey/DescribeKey). Backup still failed with PutObject AccessDenied.

They found they have a bucket policy condition requiring `aws:PrincipalArn` to match `...:role/helix-rw-private-*`, but the actual principal in S3 logs is the STS assumed-role ARN format.

They asked whether they should match on role ID or allow assumed-role ARN pattern.
2025-11-26 13:32 (Rafael Mendes, SRE) — Explained AWS nuance: S3 evaluates the principal as an assumed-role session; bucket policies should use `Principal` with the IAM role ARN (not the assumed-role session ARN), OR use `aws:PrincipalArn` with a wildcard that matches assumed-role form `arn:aws:sts::<acct>:assumed-role/<role-name>/*`.

Suggested simplest safe change:
- In bucket policy Principal, add the IAM role ARN `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/helix-rw-private-backup`
- If using conditions, avoid overly strict `aws:PrincipalArn` equality on iam role ARNs.

Also asked them to confirm whether they enforce `s3:prefix` on ListBucket; our Job does ListBucket to check existing backups / retention.
2025-11-27 08:10 (Markus Klein, Solutions) — Customer updated bucket policy to explicitly allow the IAM role and adjusted condition to accept the assumed-role pattern.

Result:
- Next scheduled run succeeded.
- They now see objects written under `prod/cluster-a/2025-11-27T08:00:03Z/`.

They asked for a final “validation checklist” they can attach to their change request evidence (security/compliance).
2025-11-27 09:05 (Rafael Mendes, SRE) — Provided validation checklist (customer-facing):
- Confirm last successful Job: `kubectl -n redwood-private get jobs | grep rw-private-backup` shows COMPLETIONS 1/1.
- Confirm artifact presence: list the latest prefix in S3 (manifest + DB dump + checksums).
- Confirm encryption: `aws s3api head-object` on manifest.json shows `ServerSideEncryption=aws:kms` and correct `SSEKMSKeyId`.
- Confirm metrics/alerting: dashboard “Private Backup/Restore” shows last_success_age < 24h and no active alerts.
- Run verify: `rw-private-dr backup verify --backup-id <id>` (if enabled) to validate checksums.

Also noted recommended follow-up hardening:
- Add an explicit KMS key policy statement allowing the backup role (least privilege).
- Ensure restore role (break-glass) is separate from backup role if they want tighter ops controls.

Link shared: SRE troubleshooting runbook + backup create/verify runbook.
2025-11-28 16:22 (Markus Klein, Solutions) — Customer confirmed they attached evidence and proceeded with upgrade gate successfully. Closing ticket.

Request for Redwood follow-up: improve docs to call out bucket policy pitfalls (PrincipalArn/assumed-role) and include the full KMS permissions block in the operator guide.
2025-11-28 16:40 (Rafael Mendes, SRE) — Resolved.

Resolution summary
- Cause: Missing KMS permissions + bucket policy condition mismatch (iam role ARN vs assumed-role ARN) for backup Job IRSA role.
- Fix: Update IAM role policy (kms Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey/DescribeKey) + update KMS key policy to trust role + adjust bucket policy principal/conditions.

Internal follow-ups
- Add docs note to Confluence + docs site: “If your bucket policy matches PrincipalArn, ensure it matches STS assumed-role format.”
- Consider adding a preflight check in `backup verify --check perms` to detect KMS permissions and bucket policy constraint patterns (tracked separately).
